name: C-Store
tagline: MIT/Brown/Brandeis research column store (VLDB 2005) that introduced projections and became Vertica.
description: C-Store was the academic column-oriented DBMS led by Michael Stonebraker with Daniel Abadi, Sam Madden and colleagues from MIT, Brown, Brandeis, UMass Boston and Yale, described in the VLDB 2005 paper "C-Store: A Column-oriented DBMS". It stored each column separately with heavy compression, organised data into overlapping sorted projections instead of base tables, split storage into a small write-optimised store and a large read-optimised store merged by a tuple mover, and used redundant projections for K-safe fault tolerance. Follow-up work used it to show the gains of executing directly on compressed columns. The team released version 0.2 of the code under a BSD license in October 2006 and stated no further releases were expected. The design was commercialised as Vertica and, with MonetDB, shaped most modern analytical column stores.
statusNote: Research prototype (2005–2006); final code release 0.2 in Oct 2006. Commercialised as Vertica.
developer: MIT, Brown, Brandeis, UMass Boston and Yale

pricing.notes: Source snapshot only; no support or further releases.

scale.notes: The paper targets a shared-nothing grid with K-safe projections; the public 0.2 code is a research snapshot for reproducing experiments.

strengths: Introduced sorted, overlapping projections as the physical design unit of a column store
Showed that operating directly on compressed columns (RLE, bit-vectors, dictionaries) pays off
Write-optimised plus read-optimised stores joined by a tuple mover, later standard in Vertica
Small, readable reference codebase under a BSD license
weaknesses: Abandoned since 2006; its authors note it no longer builds easily on modern toolchains
Never production-hardened, with limited SQL and no tooling
Released code is a research snapshot, not the full distributed design from the paper
useCases: Studying column-store internals and the origins of Vertica
notIdealFor: Any workload that needs support or updates
